To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Thursday launch handover for Inês

DRAFT — for my review before sharing

Inês,

I’m taking the train to the Netherlands tonight because my father is ill, and I’ll be with my family. I don’t know how long I’ll be away. I’m sorry to leave you with the launch at short notice, and especially with an error I only found this afternoon. The 2.1 mistake is mine, not yours; please say so if anyone asks.

I trust you completely to lead this. You know the paper as well as I do, and you ran the annex B sensitivity runs yourself. I’ve put the urgent things in order below, followed by the event details and suggested lines. Please use your judgement throughout.

1. Fix the number everywhere before the embargo lifts

The correct 2030 estimate for LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. Figure 3 and the summary had picked up the estimate from an old run in which the free allocation phase-out had not been applied. The paper’s conclusion does not change, but the headline number does.

PDF v7 on the drive is corrected on pages 3, 14 and 15. Please use that version as the source for the remaining corrections and check that it is the version being circulated.

The outstanding items are:

- Deck v4: correct slides 6 and 9, including the revenue chart on slide 9 and any affected speaker notes. Please check the rest of the deck for the old figure too.
- Embargoed press release: Hanna sent it to 34 Brussels contacts on Friday with EUR 2.1 billion in it. The embargo lifts on Thursday 26 November at 10:00 CET. Please speak to Hanna as early as possible, make sure the release is corrected, and agree how she will alert everyone who received the earlier version before the embargo lifts. Ask her to make the correction explicit rather than just quietly sending a replacement.
- If Hanna needs a senior name to sign off the corrected release, Geert knows I’m away and can do that.

Please also check any other launch copy or material being sent out for the old number. If anyone has already relied on it, we should correct it plainly.

2. Sort the press calls

Hanna told two journalists I would be available on Wednesday afternoon: one is from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. The calendar holds background calls at 14:00 and 15:00 on Wednesday 25 November, 20 minutes each, with Hanna to confirm.

Please coordinate with Hanna promptly on whether you can take the calls and have her confirm the arrangements with both journalists. Make sure she has the corrected number and release before the calls. If either time is difficult, ask her to rearrange it. The important thing is that they hear the correction before publishing, not just at the event.

3. Confirm the revised event plan and badges

Tomás’s email today changes the run of show. The event is Thursday 26 November at the European Parliament, in the Altiero Spinelli building, with the room booked by Lindqvist’s office. Guests need to be at the security entrance by 12:00; Tomás is collecting badges. Lunch is outside the room from 12:00.

Please send Tomás the final names of everyone attending from our side by Wednesday 25 November at 12:00. He says security will not admit people whose names arrive later.

MEP Lindqvist now has to leave at 13:30 because of a vote. Tomás has asked for:

- 12:30: Lindqvist’s welcome, five minutes.
- 12:35: your presentation, shortened from 20 to 15 minutes.
- 12:50: panel starts.
- At least two questions taken by Lindqvist before she leaves at 13:30.

Please confirm the revised running order with Tomás, including who will moderate and how the remaining Q&A will work after Lindqvist leaves. The original plan had Q&A at 13:40 and a 14:00 close, but we shouldn’t assume the transition has been settled. The panel is Dr Abena Owusu-Mensah, joining remotely from the Accra Trade Policy Centre; Florian Kessler of the Alliance of European Steel Users; and you in my place.

The deck has 14 slides. Once the numbers are corrected, please cut or reorder as you see fit for 15 minutes rather than trying to rush through all of them. Abena’s remote link is in the calendar invite; she tested it last week and it worked. Please still check the connection and room setup with Tomás ahead of the event.

4. Set the tone on the panel

Kessler is likely to push on the 80% pass-through assumption and resource shuffling. Don’t let him set the tone for the whole discussion. Start from the paper’s question and findings, then answer the challenges directly and openly.

On pass-through, 80% is the central case. The annex B sensitivities test 60% and 40%: the result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. You know these runs better than anyone, so there is no need to defend the central assumption as if it were the only plausible one.

On resource shuffling, we agree it is a risk. Section 5.2 addresses it, and we recommend the Commission’s monitoring report. Abena was strong on the LDC perspective in our call and may have useful points to add.

If the corrected figure comes up, I suggest keeping it simple: the earlier material used a number from an old run; the correct 2030 estimate is EUR 1.4 billion; the conclusion remains the same. The mistake was mine.

And please remember Lisbon: when the projector died at the COP side event, you rescued my panel. You are better live than you think.

5. After the launch

Lucy Tran from Halvorsen will attend with a colleague. For the grant report she has asked for two event photos and attendance numbers, ideally by 4 December. Please arrange for someone to take the photos and count attendance on the day, then make sure the material gets to Lucy. It may be easiest to ask Hanna or another colleague to own this so it doesn’t sit with you during the panel.

You can call me if you need to. After 09:00 tomorrow I might not pick up, so please don’t wait for me to make a decision or hold up a correction. If anyone asks about my absence, please keep it to: “My father is ill, and I am with my family.”

I’m sorry again for the mess and the timing. Thank you for stepping in, Inês. I know you’ll do this well.

Marieke
